subQuestions.questionText: Rural settlements are associated with … activities. (A: primary / B: secondary / C: tertiary / D: quaternary)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (primary) (1 mark)
Rural settlements are associated with primary activities such as farming, fishing, mining and forestry.

subQuestions.questionText: A dispersed settlement pattern develops when there is … (A: one dominant water source. / B: an abundance of water. / C: a narrow river valley. / D: communal ownership of land.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (an abundance of water) (1 mark)
Where water is abundant, farmsteads do not need to cluster around a single water source, so a dispersed settlement pattern develops.

subQuestions.questionText: An advantage of a rural nucleated settlement: (A: Sharing of farm equipment / B: Large, commercial plots of land / C: Making independent decisions / D: Making large profits)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (Sharing of farm equipment) (1 mark)
Because farmsteads are clustered closely together in a nucleated settlement, farmers can easily share equipment and services. The other options are advantages associated with dispersed settlements.

subQuestions.questionText: A … is the location of a settlement in relation to the surrounding area. (A: gap / B: site / C: bridging point / D: situation)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (situation) (1 mark)
Situation refers to the location of a settlement in relation to the surrounding area/features, while site refers to the actual ground on which the settlement is built.

subQuestions.questionText: A dry-point settlement is located … water because water is … (A: far from; scarce. / B: far from; a threat. / C: near; a threat. / D: near; scarce.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (far from; a threat) (1 mark)
A dry-point settlement locates away from (far from) water because the water is a threat, e.g. to avoid flooding in low-lying or marshy areas.

subQuestions.questionText: The sketch below refers to a … shaped settlement. (Refer to the sketch of the settlement in the question paper.) (A: round / B: semi-circular / C: crossroad / D: linear)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (crossroad) (1 mark)
The sketch shows a settlement that has developed at the intersection of roads, which is the defining feature of a crossroad-shaped settlement.

subQuestions.questionText: The circular shape of the settlement below is influenced by the … (Refer to the sketch of the settlement in the question paper.) (A: lake. / B: coastline. / C: terrain. / D: roads.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (lake) (1 mark)
The settlement is arranged in a circular shape around a central lake, which influences the circular form of the settlement.

subQuestions.questionText: The following physical factors determine the site of a settlement: (i) Accessibility to transport (ii) Distance to market (iii) Relief (iv) Fertile soil. (A: (i) and (ii) / B: (ii) and (iii) / C: (ii) and (iv) / D: (iii) and (iv))
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D ((iii) and (iv)) (1 mark)
Relief and fertile soil are physical (natural) factors that determine the site of a settlement. Accessibility to transport and distance to market are economic/human factors.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Process whereby an increasing percentage of the country's population is concentrated in urban areas.' (Y: urbanisation / Z: level of urbanisation)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (urbanisation) (1 mark)
Urbanisation is the process whereby an increasing percentage of a country's population becomes concentrated in urban areas.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Increase in the number of people living in urban areas.' (Y: rate of urbanisation / Z: urban growth)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (urban growth) (1 mark)
Urban growth is the increase in the actual number of people living in urban areas.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Process whereby people move from urban areas into surrounding rural areas.' (Y: centralisation / Z: counter-urbanisation)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (counter-urbanisation) (1 mark)
Counter-urbanisation is the process whereby people move from urban areas into the surrounding rural areas.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Increase in the actual physical size of an urban area.' (Y: urban expansion / Z: urban hierarchy)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (urban expansion) (1 mark)
Urban expansion is the increase in the actual physical size (area) of an urban area.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Unplanned spread of urban areas.' (Y: urban sprawl / Z: urban decay)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (urban sprawl) (1 mark)
Urban sprawl is the unplanned, uncontrolled spread of urban areas onto surrounding land.

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Decreasing number of people living in rural areas.' (Y: rural-urban migration / Z: rural depopulation)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Z (rural depopulation) (1 mark)
Rural depopulation is the decrease in the number of people living in rural areas (often as they migrate to urban areas).

subQuestions.questionText: Choose the word/term from COLUMN B that matches the statement in COLUMN A: 'Arrangement of settlements in an area from the smallest to the largest.' (Y: hierarchy / Z: metropolis)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: Y (hierarchy) (1 mark)
A settlement hierarchy is the arrangement of settlements in an area in order from the smallest to the largest.

subQuestions.questionText: What is land reform?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (CONCEPT - 1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Policy to bring about equitable distribution and access to land. (2)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the extract, what is the benefit of well-managed land reform?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- Create assets for the poor (1)
- Stabilise relationships (1)
- Promote development (1)

subQuestions.label: 1.3.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Why is land restitution considered a challenge?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Budgets/funding needs to be accessed (2)
- Legal arrangements need to be concluded (2)

subQuestions.label: 1.3.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: How does B illustrate the successful process of land restitution? (Refer to image B, 'Well managed', in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Shaking of hands (2)
- There is no fighting (2)
- Peaceful environment (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Which factors have caused the 'process of land reform' to advance too slowly?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Lack of knowledge regarding the land reform process (2)
- Poverty/Lack of income to attend meetings (2)
- Lack of appropriate documentation (2)
- Willing seller/buyer clause (2)
- Legal processes are costly (2)
- Constrained budgets of government (2)
- Government unable to provide loans (2)
- Government unable to provide equipment (2)
- Training of farmers is costly (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the social benefits of well-managed land reform for people living in rural areas.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- The change to commercial farming would create more employment opportunities (2)
- Increase in food production would alleviate poverty (2)
- Employment would decrease poverty (2)
- There would be more reconciliation among rural communities that would bring about stability (2)
- Improved services would contribute to a better quality of life (2)
- Family units would not be broken due to a decrease in rural-urban migration (2)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO characteristics of the Johannesburg CBD that is evident in the photograph. (Refer to the infographic/photograph of the CBD of Johannesburg in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for the following (2 x 1 = 2 marks):
- Tall buildings (1)
- High density of buildings (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Which land-use zone has the highest land value, as indicated on the graph? (Refer to the graph in the infographic.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: CBD (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
The graph shows that the CBD (central business district) has the highest land value.

subQuestions.questionText: How does the land value (answer to QUESTION 1.4.2) influence the building density of the CBD?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Increases (it) (2)
The high land value of the CBD increases the building density, as buildings are packed closely together and built vertically to make maximum use of the expensive land.

subQuestions.questionText: Why is the transition zone generally dilapidated despite high land values?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- It is the future expansion of the CBD (invasion and succession) (2)
- Homeowners can still get high prices for dilapidated buildings (2)
- Landlords in the transition zone are hesitant to renovate (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Why is the outlying business district (OBD) attractive for the relocation of businesses?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY THREE of the following (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
- Greater accessibility (2)
- They are located in high population density areas (markets) (2)
- Along main roads with a constant flow of traffic (2)
- Lower land values (2)
- Lower rental costs (2)
- Modern/new buildings (2)
- More parking space (2)
- Less pollution (2)
- Less crime (2)

subQuestions.questionText: What is an informal settlement?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- A settlement that has limited planning and infrastructure (2)
- No formal ownership of the land (2)
- Land that is occupied illegally (2)
- An informal structure with different building materials (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Quote a reason from the extract for the increase in the number of informal settlements in Ethekwini.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for ANY ONE of the following quotes (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- 'Rapid urbanisation' (1)
- 'government failure to deliver adequate housing' (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Why are informal settlements in Ethekwini at risk of flooding?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Locate near water sources e.g. rivers (2)
- In low-lying areas (2)
- Lack basic amenities and infrastructure (2)
- Poor drainage/storm-water systems (2)

subQuestions.questionText: How would the lack of proper roads negatively impact on emergency services to reach informal settlements in times of disasters, like floods?
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- Poor accessibility to informal settlements (2)
- Takes longer to reach the informal settlement in times of emergency (2)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, suggest measures to prevent flood-related disasters in informal settlements in the Ethekwini Municipality.
subQuestions.memoText:
PARAGRAPH question. Award 2 marks each for ANY FOUR of the following (4 x 2 = 8 marks):
- Informal settlements should be relocated to higher-lying areas (2)
- Adequate services should be provided to informal settlements (2)
- An efficient drainage system should be installed (2)
- Provide stronger building material (2)
- Provide low-cost housing (2)
- Provide better infrastructure (2)
- Access to better emergency services (2)

subQuestions.questionText: The … of a country refers to the total value of goods and services produced by the permanent inhabitants of the country. (A: gross national product / B: gross domestic product / C: balance of trade / D: trade agreement)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (gross domestic product) (1 mark)
Note: The official marking guidelines give the answer as B. (Conventionally the total value of goods and services produced by the permanent inhabitants of a country is the gross national product; award according to the official memo, which states B.)

subQuestions.questionText: South Africa's gross domestic product (GDP) enables one to compare … (A: employment rates. / B: economies of other countries. / C: standards of living. / D: imports and exports.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (economies of other countries) (1 mark)
GDP is a standard measure that enables the economies of different countries to be compared.

subQuestions.questionText: The primary economic activity that contributed the most to the GDP in 2020 and 2021: (Refer to the GDP table in the question paper.) (A: Utilities / B: Agriculture / C: Services / D: Mining)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (Mining) (1 mark)
Of the primary economic activities shown in the table, mining contributed the most to the GDP in both 2020 and 2021.

subQuestions.questionText: The tertiary economic activity that contributes the most to South Africa's GDP: (Refer to the GDP table in the question paper.) (A: Services / B: Utilities / C: Public administration / D: Transport)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (Services) (1 mark)
Of the tertiary economic activities shown in the table, services contributes the most to South Africa's GDP.

subQuestions.questionText: Construction is an example of a … economic activity. (A: primary / B: secondary / C: tertiary / D: quaternary)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (secondary) (1 mark)
Construction processes and assembles raw materials into finished structures, which makes it a secondary economic activity.

subQuestions.questionText: The economic activity that showed a decrease from 2020 to 2021: (Refer to the GDP table in the question paper.) (A: Utilities / B: Services / C: Construction / D: Agriculture)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (Agriculture) (1 mark)
According to the table, agriculture decreased from 127 960 (2020) to 114 030 (2021), while the other activities increased.

subQuestions.questionText: The economic activity that contributed the most to the secondary sector in 2021: (Refer to the GDP table in the question paper.) (A: Construction / B: Services / C: Manufacturing / D: Utilities)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (Manufacturing) (1 mark)
Manufacturing is the secondary-sector activity that contributed the most to the GDP in 2021.

subQuestions.questionText: TWO statements below are TRUE with respect to the sector contributions made to South Africa's GDP: (i) Primary sector contributes the least. (ii) Secondary sector contributes the least. (iii) Quaternary sector contributes the most. (iv) Tertiary sector contributes the most. (A: (i) and (ii) / B: (i) and (iv) / C: (ii) and (iii) / D: (i) and (iii))
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B ((i) and (iv)) (1 mark)
The primary sector contributes the least and the tertiary sector contributes the most to South Africa's GDP.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'Located close to customers.' (Choose from: Ubiquitous industries; Market-orientated industries; Raw-material-orientated industries; Heavy industries; Footloose industries; Bridge industries; Light industries)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Market orientated industries (1 mark)
Market-orientated industries locate close to their customers/market, e.g. because their goods are perishable, fragile or gain bulk during production.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'The availability of different modes of transport is important.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Bridge industries (1 mark)
Bridge (break-of-bulk) industries locate where goods are transferred between different modes of transport, so the availability of different transport modes is important.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'Need large amounts of flat land on the outskirts of built-up areas.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Heavy industries (1 mark)
Heavy industries need large amounts of flat land and locate on the outskirts of built-up areas because they occupy large spaces and cause pollution.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'Location is not determined by any specific factors.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Footloose industries (1 mark)
Footloose industries are not tied to raw materials or markets, so their location is not determined by any specific factors.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'Located in built-up areas as there is little air and noise pollution.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Light industries (1 mark)
Light industries produce small consumer goods and cause little air and noise pollution, so they can locate within built-up areas.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'Location is determined by bulky unprocessed materials.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Raw-material orientated industries (1 mark)
Raw-material-orientated industries locate near bulky, unprocessed raw materials to reduce transport costs.

subQuestions.questionText: Match the description with ONE type of industry: 'Telkom is an example of this type of industry.'
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Ubiquitous industries (1 mark)
Ubiquitous industries are widely distributed and can be located anywhere as they serve customers everywhere; Telkom (telecommunications) is given as an example.

subQuestions.questionText: Define the concept food security.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (CONCEPT - 1 x 2 = 2 marks):
When nutritious food is accessible to the people of a country. (2)

subQuestions.questionText: What percentage of South Africans experienced food insecurity in 2021? (Refer to the extract in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 23,6% (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
According to the extract, almost 23,6 per cent of South Africans were affected by moderate to severe food insecurity in 2021.

subQuestions.questionText: What is the importance of the Food Insecurity Experience Scale according to the extract?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
To make a comparison of food security across countries. (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest how health pandemics, such as Covid-19, lead to food insecurity in South Africa.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 2 = 2 marks):
- People were unable to work, reducing food production/industry (2)
- Due to unemployment people could not purchase food (2)
- Borders closed and countries could not import food (2)

subQuestions.questionText: In a paragraph of approximately EIGHT lines, explain how the South African government can assist farmers in achieving 'Zero Hunger' by 2030.
subQuestions.memoText:
PARAGRAPH question. Award 2 marks each for ANY FOUR of the following (4 x 2 = 8 marks):
- Incentives can increase productivity on farms (2)
- Technical support for small-scale farmers will increase production (2)
- Providing modernised farming equipment will increase production (2)
- Encourage (incentives) subsistence farmers (fragmented land) to embrace commercial farming (2)
- Incentives for co-operative farming will increase the variety and quantity of products (2)
- Research into a variety of farming practices will optimize production (2)
- Land reform programmes should be prioritized to give more people access to farming land (2)
- Subsidising farmers with the procurement of genetically modified (GM) crops will guarantee production of crops (2)
- Programmes to upskill farmers will improve efficiency and protect the land (2)
- Access to pesticides and insecticides improve and ensure the quality of crops (2)

subQuestions.questionText: According to the graph, state the trend in South Africa's gold production from 1970 to 2020. (Refer to the gold production infographic in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Decreased (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
South Africa's gold production shows a decreasing trend from 1970 (1 000 tons) to 2020 (101 tons).

subQuestions.questionText: How many tons of gold did South Africa produce in 2020, according to the table?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 101 (tons) (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
According to the table, South Africa produced 101 tons of gold in 2020.

subQuestions.questionText: According to the table, which country was the leading gold producer in 2020?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: China (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
According to the table, China was the leading gold producer in 2020 with 380 tons.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO physical factors that favoured South Africa as the leading producer of gold in 1970.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Witwatersrand has the largest gold reef deposit (2)
- Gold deposits are closer to the surface (2)
- Lower geothermal gradient (2)
- Gold reserves are of a high quality (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO factors that resulted in a reduction of gold production from 1990 to 2020.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Strike action (2)
- Labour disputes (2)
- Decreased foreign investment in the mines (2)
- Certain mines have had to close down permanently (2)
- High numbers of unskilled miners (2)
- Threat of nationalisation (2)
- Power outages (load shedding) (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how a reduction in South Africa's gold production will impact negatively on its economic growth.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- An increase in unemployment will reduce buying power (2)
- Reduced market and business profits will decrease (2)
- Less taxes paid to government will reduce budgets for the development of infrastructure (2)
- Decrease in the multiplier effect in the country, resulting in all sectors of the economy being affected (2)
- Decrease in foreign income due to less gold exports causes economic recession (2)
- Some mines would be forced to close, decreasing the GDP of the country (2)

subQuestions.questionText: What is an industrial development zone?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer (CONCEPT - 1 x 2 = 2 marks):
Focussed industrial development area that creates jobs and promotes exports, close to major transport routes with international links. (2)

subQuestions.questionText: What transport infrastructure makes the Dube TradePort IDZ unique compared to other IDZs in South Africa, according to the fact file?
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: It is the largest Greenfield airport development (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
According to the fact file, the Dube TradePort is the largest greenfield airport development in Africa and the only one in South Africa.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO factors on the map that resulted in greater accessibility to the Dube TradePort IDZ. (Refer to the Dube TradePort infographic/map in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 1 = 2 marks):
- Harbour (1)
- N2 (1)
- King Shaka (International Airport) (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe TWO advantages regarding infrastructure that the Dube TradePort IDZ could offer to attract industries.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY TWO of the following (2 x 2 = 4 marks):
- Access to improved telecommunication services (2)
- Available infrastructure (2)
- Airport provides industries with access to local and international markets (2)
- Access to power supply (2)
- Dams ensure an abundance of water (2)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how the Dube TradePort IDZ would upskill (improve) labour in the province.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 2 marks each for ANY THREE of the following (3 x 2 = 6 marks):
- A variety of industries would expose labourers to a variety of skills (2)
- Technical specialists from other countries would transfer skills to the local labour force (2)
- Local labour would acquire Fourth Industrial Revolution skills which would keep them abreast of the latest technological development (2)
- The success of the Dube TradePort IDZ would ensure a more permanent/stable labour force (2)

subQuestions.questionText: The contour interval of the orthophoto map is (5 m/20 m). (Refer to the orthophoto map.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 5 m (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
The contour interval of the 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map is 5 m.

subQuestions.questionText: Which vertical exaggeration would give the most detailed indication of the landforms on a cross-section? (A: 2 times / B: 5 times / C: 10 times / D: 20 times)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (20 times) (1 mark)
The largest vertical exaggeration (20 times) stretches the vertical scale the most and therefore gives the most detailed indication of the landforms on a cross-section.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Complete the grid reference/coordinates of spot height 114 in block C3 on the topographic map. Write down only the information that is not included in the question. (a) __° 37 42''S
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 29 (°) (1) (1 mark)
The latitude of spot height 114 is 29° 37' 42''S.

subQuestions.label: 3.1.3(b)
subQuestions.questionText: Complete the grid reference/coordinates of spot height 114 in block C3 on the topographic map. Write down only the information that is not included in the question. (b) 31° __ __''E
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: 04 (') (1); 47 (accept range 45–49) ('') (1) (2 marks)
The longitude of spot height 114 is 31° 04' 47''E (accept 45''–49'').

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate the average gradient between F and G. Use the following information: Vertical interval (VI): 119 m − 80 m = 39 m. (Refer to the topographic map.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award marks for steps in the calculation (4 x 1 = 4 marks):
Formula: Gradient = Vertical Interval (VI) ÷ Horizontal Equivalent (HE)
HE = 4,5 (1) cm x 500 m = 2 250 (1) m (range: 4,4–4,6 cm x 500 = 2 200–2 300)
Gradient = 39 ÷ 2 250 (1 for correct substitution)
= 1 : 57,69 (1) (range: 1 : 56,41 – 1 : 58,97)

subQuestions.questionText: Determine if the gradient between (F to G) is steeper or gentler than (H to I).
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: More gentle (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
The gradient between F and G is more gentle than the gradient between H and I.

subQuestions.questionText: Is the settlement pattern at J dispersed or nucleated? (Refer to J in block D4 on the topographic map.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Dispersed (1) (1 x 1 = 1 mark)
The settlement pattern at J is dispersed, with farmsteads spread far apart.

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE site factor that favoured farming in this area. (Refer to J in block D4 on the topographic map.)
subQuestions.memoText:

subQuestions.questionText: How does the spacing of the contour lines indicate that residential area K is built on steep/hilly land?

The contour lines are close together, which indicates steep/hilly land.

subQuestions.questionText: How did the steep/hilly land influence the type of street pattern in this area on the topographic map?

It resulted in an irregular street pattern (2)
The steep/hilly land forced roads to follow the contours, producing an irregular street pattern.

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to Canelands (6) in block A5 on the orthophoto map and state ONE situation factor that influenced the location of this industrial area.
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- Access to roads (1)
- Available labour (1)
- Easy access to markets (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE tertiary activity that is associated with the Hazelmere Dam. (Refer to the Hazelmere Dam in block A1 and an enlarged extract of the topographic map.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Award 1 mark for ANY ONE of the following (1 x 1 = 1 mark):
- Provision of water (1)
- Tourism/recreational activities (1)

subQuestions.questionText: How does this tertiary activity (answer to QUESTION 3.2.8) contribute to the economy of Verulam?
subQuestions.memoText:

Provision of water:

- Water will encourage agriculture (2)
Tourism/Recreation:

subQuestions.label: 3.3.1(a)
subQuestions.questionText: Identify the following on the sketch representing block D5 on the topographic map: (a) Human-made polygon (area) feature.
subQuestions.memoText:
Expected answer: Cultivated land (1) (1 mark)
The human-made polygon (area) feature is the cultivated land.
